title: Joseph’s strength lies in his calling, and the church must support it
setting: This revelation came to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. The church was less than four months old. In late June and early July, Joseph was arrested twice near Colesville, New York, and released both times. When he and Oliver went back to confirm new converts, a mob drove them away. The revelation was one of three given in this tense period, and its exact day is not recorded.
summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he was called to write the Book of Mormon and has been delivered from his enemies. It says he is not excused for his sins, but he should go and sin no more. After he sows and secures his fields, he is to visit the branches at Colesville, Fayette, and Manchester. If they receive him they will be blessed; if not, they will be cursed. His work is to pray, write what the Comforter gives, and expound the scriptures. Verse 9 says he will not have strength in temporal labors, because that is not his calling. Oliver is to keep declaring the gospel to the church and the world. Both men are to work miracles only when asked, take no purse or scrip, and let the church supply their needs.

contextNote.title: Strength found in the calling itself
contextNote.text: Joseph had a farm at Harmony and a young church spread across three New York towns. Verse 9 settles which work comes first. It says he will not have strength in temporal labors, “for this is not thy calling”. Verse 3 still lets him sow and secure his fields before he travels. It then makes the branches responsible for supporting him. Verse 18 repeats the pattern: the church will give him food, clothing, and money “in the very hour”. Here “magnify thine office” means giving his main strength to expounding scripture and confirming the churches.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 23–26 cites verses 1 and 8: the Savior can lift us “up out of” our afflictions. Verse 8 pairs “thou shalt have many” afflictions with “I am with thee”; how does verse 1 help explain why Joseph could trust that promise?
reviewNote: Read all 19 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, July 1830, to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery, after persecution forced partial seclusion. JSP historical introduction read for the two trials (South Bainbridge, 1 July; Colesville, about 2 July), the mob at the attempted confirmations, and Oliver’s trip to Fayette. JSP notes the word July was inserted later and the exact day is unknown; it was likely dictated before Oliver left in mid-July. Fact-check 2026-10-12: ldsText now states the lesson’s actual teaching on section 24 (the Savior lifts us out of afflictions, vv. 1, 8).
